newsitem.title: IRAN: Qatar foreign minister arrives in Iran for talks.
newsitem.headline: Qatar foreign minister arrives in Iran for talks.

text.p: Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani arrived in Tehran on Saturday for a one-day visit to discuss Gulf security with Iranian leaders, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
The agency quoted Sheikh Hamad as saying the visit was one a series of regular meetings between Iran and Qatar.
"(Sheikh Hamad) said security in the Persian Gulf is of vital importance for all littoral states, requiring their full cooperation," IRNA said.

"(Iranian) Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati, greeting his Qatari counterpart, told reporters the current visit was part of a regular exchange of visits between officials of the two countries held to discuss bilateral relations and regional development," IRNA said.
Sheikh Hamad is also expected to meet President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani during his brief stay.
Qatar, a small oil and gas-rich country, regards non-Arab Iran as an important regional power with whom it maintains close political and economic relations.
Iran, whose influence in the region diminished after the 1979 fall of the late shah, has been trying to improve ties with Qatar and other Gulf Arab states.
In May, Qatar politely declined an Iranian offer of a defence pact, saying it was not necessary at that stage.
